evidence.paraphrase: Mudgala says Jambū’s ruler has nine sons Nābhi, Kimpuruṣa, Hari, Ilāvṛta, Hiraṇmaya, Kuru, Ramya, Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla; he gives each an eponymous region. Father is called Jambū ruler here, not named; prior 10.4 identifies him as Āgnīdhra. The SEVEN Priyavrata sons, distinct from these nine grandsons, then enter forest, perform tapas, become Gaṇapatyas/Brahman-knowers and at the end attain Gaṇeśa’s abode without return through yoga-nondifference.
evidence.verifier: Mudgala continuation5 author, direct Sanskrit body
evidence.verification_notes: Read actual cited body; attributed dialogue kept distinct from narrator fact. Independent root review pending.

evidence.paraphrase: Jambū has one-lakh-yojana extent and a surrounding salt ocean. In its middle is golden Meru, with varied minerals/herbs, good-water rivers, caves and creatures.

evidence.paraphrase: 8–9 gives Meru utsedha one lakh, then 60000 measurement associated with bahis-sthiti, 32000 associated with adhas-sthiti and 8000 yojanas samantataḥ. Exact dimensional allocation and apparent inconsistency remain unresolved; no remembered standard Meru dimensions substituted.

evidence.paraphrase: Meru stands above/below earth’s middle, lotus-shaped, with surrounding mineral-rich lotus-petal-like mountains. Gods, Guhyakas, birds, yogins, Rākṣasas, siddhas, Nāga chiefs, sages, Gandharvas, Piśācas/Bhūtas dwell there; gardens for gods and waters remove age/sorrow. Eight chief mountains beginning Kailāsa stand in directions with Rudra and direction-lords; central great forest is Brahmā’s place. Nine Jambū regions: three south, three north, two east/west, one central; Himācala and other mountains bound them.

evidence.paraphrase: Nābhi’s region Ajanābha lies near Himācala and is karma-ground. Actions there send people to other islands/regions/Pātāla/heavens to enjoy fruit; after enjoyment they return here for acts. Sin sends men/women to hell, then back. Yoga there makes yogin and devotion gives Gaṇapatya nature, so this region called Himalayan is esteemed highest/all-giving, though relatively little pleasure, heat/cold and many diseases. Four varṇas and mixed/different dharmas, yuga measures/duties and diverse self-interested dispositions occur here.

evidence.paraphrase: Vindhya, Sahyādri and many mountains arise with rivers from them. Sweet river waters give merit by mere bathing; inhabitants act with threefold conduct. Divine tīrthas/Brahmin places give greater act-born fruits to servants. This Ajanābha region is called Bhārata because it bears karma. Mudgala closes the brief earth-circle account; hearing/reading removes sins. This etymology does not assert a king Bhārata ancestry not narrated here.

evidence.paraphrase: Mudgala describes seven cosmic-egg worlds Bhūr, Bhuvar, Svar, Mahar, Jana, Tapo, Satya. Bhūr is the walking-accessible seven-island region illuminated by Sun/Moon; Bhuvar runs from Bhūr to Sun, Svar from Sun to Dhruva with corresponding Bhūr extent. Eight Vāyu divisions are Āvaha, Pravaha, Annavaha, Saṃvaha, Vivaha, Parāvaha, Parivaha, Vaha. Distance sequence in yojanas: Earth→Sun 100000, Sun→Moon 100000, Moon→stars 100000, stars→planet zone 200000, planet zone→ṛṣi zone 100000, ṛṣi zone→Dhruva 100000. Dhruva is axis of luminary wheel, holding wind-rays and moving stars. These are source cosmography, not modern astronomical measurements.

evidence.paraphrase: Sun maṇḍala extent 10000 and Moon 12000 yojanas; Rāhu 10000 below Sun, maṇḍala 13000. Darkness-formed Rāhu moves at parvan and rapidly covers Sun/Moon with shadow; called eclipse. Bhārgava’s maṇḍala is 1/16 Moon; Bṛhaspati 1/4 less than Bhārgava; Bhauma/Saura 1/4 less than Bṛhaspati; Saumya 1/4 less than those. Star/nakṣatra maṇḍalas successively 500/400/300/200, smallest star 1 ½ yojanas. Fractions preserved as stated, without calculated replacements.

Ordering upward: Sun, Moon, stars, Kavi/Bhārgava, Budha, Bhauma, Bṛhaspati, Śanaiścara, seven ṛṣis, Dhruva. Sun travels two ayanas and governs planets. Bhauma is above Soma’s son, referring to Budha; only this explicit patronymic is normalized as parenthood, not an invented Bhārgava/Bṛhaspati family.

evidence.paraphrase: Sun chariot 9000 yojanas and shaft twice that; axle one lakh anchored at Dhruva, second axle’s wheel on Mānasā mountain. Wheel is zodiac/twelve-spoked; seven horses are metres led by Gāyatrī. Southward ayana is fast, northward slow. On Mānasā are east Indra’s Amarāvatī, south Dharmarāja’s Saṃyamanī, west Varuṇa’s Sukhā, north Kubera’s Vibhā. Sun dawn at Indra city, midday Yama, evening Varuṇa, midnight Kubera; potter-wheel-like movement gives direction-dependent perceived times.

narrative_events.details: Mudgala says Jambū’s ruler has nine sons Nābhi, Kimpuruṣa, Hari, Ilāvṛta, Hiraṇmaya, Kuru, Ramya, Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla; he gives each an eponymous region. Father is called Jambū ruler here, not named; prior 10.4 identifies him as Āgnīdhra. The SEVEN Priyavrata sons, distinct from these nine grandsons, then enter forest, perform tapas, become Gaṇapatyas/Brahman-knowers and at the end attain Gaṇeśa’s abode without return through yoga-nondifference.
Jambū has one-lakh-yojana extent and a surrounding salt ocean. In its middle is golden Meru, with varied minerals/herbs, good-water rivers, caves and creatures.

Meru stands above/below earth’s middle, lotus-shaped, with surrounding mineral-rich lotus-petal-like mountains. Gods, Guhyakas, birds, yogins, Rākṣasas, siddhas, Nāga chiefs, sages, Gandharvas, Piśācas/Bhūtas dwell there; gardens for gods and waters remove age/sorrow. Eight chief mountains beginning Kailāsa stand in directions with Rudra and direction-lords; central great forest is Brahmā’s place. Nine Jambū regions: three south, three north, two east/west, one central; Himācala and other mountains bound them.

Regions have varied mountains/rivers and happy inhabitants. Eight regions excluding Ajanābha have stable natural siddhi, eternally youthful beautiful men/women enjoying like gods, good qualities/mutual attachment, equal time/enjoyment, varṇa/āśrama dharma and compassion; no changing yuga-dharma or heat/cold suffering.

Nābhi’s region Ajanābha lies near Himācala and is karma-ground. Actions there send people to other islands/regions/Pātāla/heavens to enjoy fruit; after enjoyment they return here for acts. Sin sends men/women to hell, then back. Yoga there makes yogin and devotion gives Gaṇapatya nature, so this region called Himalayan is esteemed highest/all-giving, though relatively little pleasure, heat/cold and many diseases. Four varṇas and mixed/different dharmas, yuga measures/duties and diverse self-interested dispositions occur here.

Vindhya, Sahyādri and many mountains arise with rivers from them. Sweet river waters give merit by mere bathing; inhabitants act with threefold conduct. Divine tīrthas/Brahmin places give greater act-born fruits to servants. This Ajanābha region is called Bhārata because it bears karma. Mudgala closes the brief earth-circle account; hearing/reading removes sins. This etymology does not assert a king Bhārata ancestry not narrated here.

Mudgala describes seven cosmic-egg worlds Bhūr, Bhuvar, Svar, Mahar, Jana, Tapo, Satya. Bhūr is the walking-accessible seven-island region illuminated by Sun/Moon; Bhuvar runs from Bhūr to Sun, Svar from Sun to Dhruva with corresponding Bhūr extent. Eight Vāyu divisions are Āvaha, Pravaha, Annavaha, Saṃvaha, Vivaha, Parāvaha, Parivaha, Vaha. Distance sequence in yojanas: Earth→Sun 100000, Sun→Moon 100000, Moon→stars 100000, stars→planet zone 200000, planet zone→ṛṣi zone 100000, ṛṣi zone→Dhruva 100000. Dhruva is axis of luminary wheel, holding wind-rays and moving stars. These are source cosmography, not modern astronomical measurements.

Sun maṇḍala extent 10000 and Moon 12000 yojanas; Rāhu 10000 below Sun, maṇḍala 13000. Darkness-formed Rāhu moves at parvan and rapidly covers Sun/Moon with shadow; called eclipse. Bhārgava’s maṇḍala is 1/16 Moon; Bṛhaspati 1/4 less than Bhārgava; Bhauma/Saura 1/4 less than Bṛhaspati; Saumya 1/4 less than those. Star/nakṣatra maṇḍalas successively 500/400/300/200, smallest star 1 ½ yojanas. Fractions preserved as stated, without calculated replacements.

Three distant slow planets named Saura, Aṅgirā, Bhauma lie above four fast planets Sun, Moon, Budha, Bhārgava. Ordering upward: Sun, Moon, stars, Kavi/Bhārgava, Budha, Bhauma, Bṛhaspati, Śanaiścara, seven ṛṣis, Dhruva. Sun travels two ayanas and governs planets. Bhauma is above Soma’s son, referring to Budha; only this explicit patronymic is normalized as parenthood, not an invented Bhārgava/Bṛhaspati family.

Sun chariot 9000 yojanas and shaft twice that; axle one lakh anchored at Dhruva, second axle’s wheel on Mānasā mountain. Wheel is zodiac/twelve-spoked; seven horses are metres led by Gāyatrī. Southward ayana is fast, northward slow. On Mānasā are east Indra’s Amarāvatī, south Dharmarāja’s Saṃyamanī, west Varuṇa’s Sukhā, north Kubera’s Vibhā. Sun dawn at Indra city, midday Yama, evening Varuṇa, midnight Kubera; potter-wheel-like movement gives direction-dependent perceived times.

Sun rays sustain people and fill three worlds, making day/night. Water, earth and sky and whole god/demon/human world arise, are supported and end in Sun. Enumerated deities, stars, fire, plants, Brahmins/water draw their radiance from him; he distributes all brilliance for play. Prabhākara is all-self/lord, Gaṇeśa portion, root of three worlds and karma-formed deity. This is source cosmological praise/support, not a universal biological genealogy.

Twelve other Bhānus arise as Sun kalāṃśas and shine from chariot in 12 months/seasonal order beginning spring: Dhātā, Aryamā, Mitra, Varuṇa, Śakra, Vivasvān, Pūṣā, Parjanya, Aṃśu, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Viṣṇu. Their source-qualified solar manifestation roles are distinguished from same-name gods/lineages; no biological parentage inferred.

Twelve sages praise Sun with metres: Pulastya, Pulaha, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Aṅgiras, Bhṛgu, Bharadvāja, Gautama, Kaśyapa, Kratu, Jamadagni, Kauśika. Grāmaṇī rein-holders: Rathakṛt, Rathaujas, Rathacitra, Svabāhuka, Rathasvana, Varuṇa, Suṣeṇa, Senajit, Tārkṣya, Ariṣṭanemi, Rathajit, Satyajit. Same-name Grāmaṇī Varuṇa is not silently identified with water-lord/solar portion.

Twelve Rākṣasa leaders advance before Sun: Heti, Praheti, Pauruṣeya, Vadha, Sarpa, Vyāghra, Vyādha, Vāta, Vidyut, Divākara, Brahmopeta, Yajñopeta. Nāgas carrying Sun across 12 months: Vāsuki, Kaṅkanīra, Takṣaka, Elāpatra, Śaṅkhapāla, Airāvata, Dhanañjaya, Mahāpadma, Karkoṭaka, Kambala, Aśvatara. Eleven Nāga names actually present; no twelfth filled from another text. Serpent Airāvata/Rākṣasa Divākara are not merged with same-name elephant/Sun.

Twelve singing Gandharvas: Tumburu, Nārada, Hāhā, Hūhū, Viśvāvasu, Ugrasena, Vasuruci, Avīvasu, Citrasena, Ūrṇāyu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Sūryavarcā. Twelve dancing Apsarases: Ghanastanī, Rambhā, Puñjikasthalī, Menakā, Sahajanyā, Pramlocā, Anumlocā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, Urvaśī, Pūrvacitti, Tilottamā; they delight Sun in seasonal order. Nārada retains issued source-local identity with this attributed singing role, no biological status change.

Sages hymn, Gandharvas/Apsarases sing/dance, Grāmaṇī Yakṣa-like beings hold reins, serpents carry and Yātudhānas advance. Vālakhilyas escort Sun rising→setting. Attendants heat/rain/shine/blow/create, remove evil acts when recounted, travel in wind-speed wish-moving vimāna, nourish/protect at yuga end. Sun assumes their forms, makes day/night, nourishes Pitṛs/gods/humans and is Gaṇeśa portion/time-self. Other 8 planets bind to Dhruva by wind-rays and receive Sun nourishment.

Moon three-wheel chariot has 10 jasmine-white horses left/right; star pathways and Dhruva support with waxing/waning. Sun Suṣumna ray replenishes Moon nectar drunk by gods in sequence over half-month. With little fifteenth-part remaining, Pitṛs attend in afternoon and drink for 2 LAVAS; remaining kalā is svadhā nectar issued through rays at amāvāsyā, giving monthly satisfaction. Moon does not perish from nectar drinking; Sun causes waxing/waning. No lava-to-modern-time conversion.

Budha/Soma-son chariot 4 wind-speed LIONS; Bhārgava golden 8 horses; Bhauma 8 RAMS; Bṛhaspati golden 8 REDhorses; Manda iron 8 BLUEvultures; Svarbhānu/Rāhu black lions and Ketu doves, counts unspecified. All 9 planet/star stations bind Dhruva by wind-rays; he revolves and moves them in every direction. No remembered horse substitutions.

Successive higher worlds each one-KOṬI-yojana apart: Dhruva→Mahar (kalpa-authorized enjoyers), Mahar→Jana (Sanaka-led sages in trasareṇu vimānas), Jana→Tapo (fearless Vairāja gods), Tapo→Satya (returnless Brahmā residence). Brahmā/yogins drink yoga nectar there; renouncers, constant brahmacārins, vow/tapas/siddha/sacrifice practitioners dwell. It is flaming gate for yogins going to supreme Gaṇeśa; beyond is unsupported/world-form-free. Cosmic-egg Virāṭ form extends through Satya.

Śakti world 2 koṭiyojanas beyond Brahmā world, unsupported luminous Mahāmāyā setting, 10000-yojana extent. Desireless Śakti devotees/yogins attain it. Resident Śaktis create same-form men by own brilliance and play with them in female form. This is cosmic manifestation/play, not ordinary biological procreation.

Solar world 4 koṭiyojanas beyond Śakti world, unsupported/eternal/luminous, extent equal to Śakti world. Sun-residents by śuklagati and desireless Sun devotees arrive, as radiant as Sun. Male-form Sun creates karma-māyā Saṃjñā from LEFT LIMB and continually plays with her. This solar-world origin is recorded alongside earlier 1.17’s Śakti-heart origin, without a single biological-birth claim or chronology harmonization.

Viṣṇu/Vikuṇṭha world 8 koṭiyojanas beyond Solar world, 10000-yojana extent, unsupported/eternal/luminous. Desireless devoted Vaiṣṇavas attain perpetual happiness and freely moving women/men reside. Viṣṇu creates Bhogalakṣmī from LEFT and Muktilakṣmī from RIGHT and plays in twofold māyā. Mukti form not automatically identified with Datta’s specifically manifested Mokṣalakṣmī.

Śaṅkara/Kailāsa world 16 koṭiyojanas beyond Viṣṇu world, 10000 extent, unsupported, luminous, delusion-free/happy. Desireless Śiva devotees arrive. Śiva plays by yoga: left is Prakṛti, right Puruṣa, their union ānanda; Nārāyaṇa-mayī Śakti and half-female/half-male Śiva. He separates that Śakti into THREE forms, unnamed here, and continually plays, delusion-free yet māyā-supporting. No three remembered goddess names or new biological spousal genealogy imported.

Beyond that Mahī lies Svānanda Brahman, described as supreme state in this teaching. Self-experienced Brahman is fourfold: Śiva unmanifest/neti/nirmoha, Viṣṇu sama, Sun self, Śakti asat; their nondifference/union is Svānanda. Every principle has its own Svānanda, with varied Brahmans such as space supporting successive hierarchy. Full Gaṇapati Svānanda is all-union samādhi; Gaṇeśa abides in each own-bliss as kalāṃśa for play and all siddhis. Hearing the briefly told higher worlds gives all wishes; no exact beyond-Mahī distance supplied.

Seven nether regions descending: Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Talātala, Mahātala, Rasātala, Pātāla. Atala dusky, 10000 yojanas below Earth and 100000 extent; unnamed Maya-son, Namuci and Nāgas inhabit. Vitala white, 10000 below, inhabited by Nāga/Asuras Kambala, Śaṅkukarṇa, Hayagrīva, Jumbhaka. Sutala yellow similarly below, with Vainateya-led birds, Bali, Kālanemi and other fearless Nāga/demons. Vainateya patronymic retained for Garuḍa without an unstated father.

Talātala gravelly with Mayāsura, Bāṇa, Andhaka, Kālakeya and Nivātakavaca groups and carefree Nāgas. Mahātala black with Takṣaka/Nāgas and thousands of Hiraṇyapura-based demons fearless of gods. Rasātala stone-made, below, with Vāsuki-led Nāgas/demons, luminous sharp poisonous inhabitants. Pātāla blue, Śeṣa’s purposeful station; demons/gods/Nāgas worship the Nāga lord devotedly.

Śeṣa stands 30000 yojanas below Pātāla, Gaṇeśa devotee/portion, Viṣṇu kalāvatāra and called Kālarudra. Thousand-faced, powerful, poison-born flame burns entire world; deathless hence Ananta, he dissolves at Brahmā-day’s end and remains. Vāsuki-led Nāga kings, Prahlāda-led demons and Nāga women serve him; women worship for many desired successes, not a narrated grant of all requests.

1000 yojanas below Śeṣa is Viṣṇu’s tortoise/Kūrma station, served by Varuṇa and others;1000 further below is Viṣṇu’s Varāha, served by Earth and others, giving fearlessness to devotees. Whole structure rests on Śeṣa; Śeṣa rests on Kūrma, Kūrma on Varāha. Unsupported Varāha remembers Gaṇeśa in heart and by that power supports all. No battle or Earth-lifting episode supplied here.

Below Varāha are purifying/punishing hells Raurava, Tāmisra, Mahāraurava, Andhatāmisra, Sūcīmukha, Lohadaṇḍa, Taptavāluka, Khaḍgapatraka, Lālāsya, Kṛmibhakṣya and many others, where sinners are cooked. Mudgala says the cosmic sphere cannot be fully expanded here; Dakṣa’s curse-delusion will end by Gaṇeśa worship and he will know truly. All cosmic eggs alike have 8 envelopes and Guṇeśa support; this is Gaṇapati’s egg-form briefly told. Devoted hearing/reading gives all, siddhis, enjoyment/liberation and sin-cover destruction.
